Definition: adverb from G3650; completely, i.e. altogether; (by analogy), everywhere; (negatively) not by any means:--at all, commonly, utterly.
BiblicalUsage: The word hólōs is at all, commonly, utterly — a small word, used 4 times; Matthew and 1 Corinthians show it in use.
TheologicalSignificance: I read hólōs plainly: at all, commonly, utterly, and I leave it there.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
